page: Microsoft Azure E16ads_v5 is an EADSv5-family virtual machine configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz, the instance features 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. The server includes 614 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core testing placing in the top 25% at 2702.68. Passmark memory testing also demonstrates strong performance. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is a notable tradeoff, with read-only large block bandwidth at 38.7 GB/sec and write large block bandwidth at 22.85 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, software compilation, and database operations consistently register in the average range.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high memory density relative to the vCPU count allows memory-intensive workloads to run without the overhead of provisioning excess compute resources. This hardware profile is suitable for database operations, caching layers such as Redis, web serving, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
